[MUQATIL:39:55-60/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | A further regretful claim is that, had God guided the speaker, he would have been among the God-fearing.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An أن-clause may be syntactically built on a preceding expression such as أحقا; reversing it to إن would wrongly begin إن where it is not licensed.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أما بعد فإن الله is like أما اليوم فإنك; بعد is otherwise ungoverned when neither annexed nor built on another expression.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | شد ما أنك ذاهب and عز ما أنك ذاهب mean حقا أنك ذاهب, like أما أنك ذاهب; they may also be parsed on the analogy of نعم ما.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After لو, a nominal clause normally cannot begin directly except with أن; لولا, by contrast, can be followed by nouns. | mentions 17:100
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | فريق may be singular while referring to a group, like صديق; the following Quranic قعيد is cited as a comparable singular form in a paired setting.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In كما أنه لا يعلم and كما أنك هاهنا, the كاف governs أن and ما is extra; it is retained to keep the wording distinct from كأن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetry may omit ما from the construction, just as it may omit ما in إما; Sībawayh cites al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī as evidence.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | reports | Yunus reports that Arabs recited al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur’s أحقا أن example; al-Khalil treats its threat as occupying the same syntactic position as الرحيل بعد غد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Al-ʿAbdī, ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa, and al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī each supply poetic attestations of the أحقا/أن construction.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalil explains that تهددكم here functions like الرحيل بعد غد, with أن in its corresponding position.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The raised construction أحقا أن and أكبر ظنك أن is strong; one may also make the latter clause the first element of the construction.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In لا محالة أنك ذاهب, أن depends on an elided من, as in لا محالة من أنك ذاهب; this avoids reversing the clause.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أما permits إن after it because it carries the sense مهما يكن من شيء; thus أما حقا فإنك ذاهب and أما يوم الجمعة فإنك ذاهب are sound.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With أما في الدار, فإنك قائم works only if the following clause is presented as a report; for the intended location meaning, say فأنت قائم.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أما جهد رأيي فأنك ذاهب is permitted; فإنك is weaker because the phrase need not be construed as making effort an adverbial setting for the proposition.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأنتكونأنفيهمبنيةعلىماقبلها)#504/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أما اليوم أنك مرتحل means الرحلة في اليوم; a temporal phrase may thus precede the أن-clause.
[MUSNAD-AHMAD:10652/r1] MUSNAD-AHMAD, d. 241 · أبو هريرة | reports | Abu Hurayra reports that the people of Hell regret, “If God had guided me,” while the people of Paradise thank God for guidance, illustrating the regret voiced in the verse.
[MUSNAD-AHMAD:21589/r1] MUSNAD-AHMAD, d. 241 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Asked about predestination, Ubayy, Hudhayfa, Ibn Masud, and Zayd convey that belief in God's decree is required and that God may justly punish all; this bears on the verse's appeal to divine guidance.
[MUSNAD-AHMAD:21611/r1] MUSNAD-AHMAD, d. 241 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The Prophet says that belief in predestination is required: whatever befalls a person could not have missed them, and vice versa; God is not unjust if He punishes creation.
[MUSNAD-AHMAD:21653/r1] MUSNAD-AHMAD, d. 241 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Ubayy and other Companions tell Ibn al-Daylami that belief in predestination is essential and that God's mercy exceeds deeds; Zayd identifies the teaching as from the Prophet.
[TAB-FULL:v20p236/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The commands to repent and submit aim to prevent three afterlife regrets: sorrow for neglect, a claim that God did not guide, and a wish to return and act righteously.
[TAB-FULL:v20p236/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The speaker imagines saying that, had God guided her to truth and right direction, she would have been pious through obedience and following His pleasure.

[ZAJJAJ:v4p358/r13] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The following speeches likewise name what people would regret saying; God had already made the paths of guidance clear, and a living person capable of discernment has been given the proof.
[NAHHAS:v4p17/r11] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | One view wishes God had guided the speaker to safety from the Fire and returned him to earthly obligation so he could avoid sins.
[NAHHAS:v4p17/r12] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | reports | Another view refers to guidance in worldly life.

[THALABI:v8p246/r13] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The lost person imagines that divine guidance would have made him God-fearing, then wishes for another return to worldly life so he could be among the virtuous.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p136/r1] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | A cited poetic example states the object of wishing explicitly because the point cannot be made without it; wishing to weep and producing contemplation instead are distinct acts, so the result cannot explain the wish's omitted object.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p136/r2] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | In other cases, the object of wishing or intending may be omitted because the answer introduced by لو and its sisters supplies it.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p136/r3] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · البحتري | holds | In the Buthuri line, لك مثلا is omitted from قد طلبنا because the following clause لم نجد لك مثلا supplies it, and the omission adds subtle force.
[JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p136/r4] JURJANI-DALAIL, d. 471 · author | holds | The poem is stronger when the explicit word مثلا receives the denial of existence; reversing the clauses leaves the denial on a pronoun, which never matches the direct expression.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p129#2/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The soul imagines it would have been among the God-fearing had God guided it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p537#2/r12] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The two later occurrences of aw taqūlu coordinate with the first an taqūla clause.

[TABRISI:39:56-60/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | reports | One view says they neglected proofs and Qurʾān for worldly distractions, presumed God had not guided them, and are rebutted by His signs.
[TABRISI:39:56-60/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · الجبائي | reports | Al-Jubbāʾī says they mean guidance to salvation by return to worldly accountability, though on Judgment Day they know God guided them.
[TABRISI:39:56/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | ‘My signs came to you’ answers the implied negative in ‘if God had guided me’; balā answers the negative sense though unstated.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p193/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The soul claims that, had God guided it to His religion, it would have been among those who avoid shirk.
[QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r19] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The soul means that, had God guided it to His religion, it would have avoided idolatry and sins; al-Qurṭubī calls the statement itself truthful.
[QURTUBI-FULL:39:56-58/r20] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Al-Qurṭubī links this excuse to the polytheists’ claim that they would not have associated partners if God had willed. | mentions 6:148
[QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The cited polytheists say they would not have associated partners had God willed; al-Qurṭubī calls this a true phrase used for a false purpose. | mentions 6:148
[QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · علي | reports | Al-Qurṭubī compares this to ʿAlī’s judgment on the Khārijites’ slogan that judgment belongs only to God: a true phrase used for a false purpose.
[QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda distinguishes three groups: one regrets neglecting God’s affair, another says God should have guided it, and the third wishes for another return to become righteous.
[QURTUBI-FULL:39:57-59/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjāj explains

 balā as answering the implicit denial in “if God had guided me”: the speaker’s premise is “He did not guide me,” and God answers that His signs had come.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The claim that God should have guided the sinner by compulsion is outside divine wisdom; other excuses are that he was unfit for grace or ignored revelation already given.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p213/r16] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The sinner's claim is evasive and useless, like blaming leaders and devils, as in the cited line لو هدانا الله لهديناكم. | mentions 14:21
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p214/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari explains that the sinner's three statements retain their order—regret, excuse about guidance, then wish to return—and the reply answers the one requiring an answer.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p110/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God says that even if the condemned were returned, they would not follow guidance but would resume what they were forbidden, and their claim is false. | mentions 6:28

[BIQAI-FULL:v6p463/r17] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The speaker claims guidance would have made them persist among the God-fearing, who do not act without evidence directing them.

[ALUSI-FULL:v24p18/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The speaker claims that if God had guided him, he would have been among those guarded from idolatry and sins.
